We need to find a template that when applied retrosynthetically (i.e., reverse of SN2) to the given molecule yields a precursor with a halide (leaving group) and a nucleophile (maybe OH, OR, CN). The description: "C-N formed and C-Cl gone breaking a 'halide' functional group". So forward reaction: nucleophile (e.g., CN) attacks alkyl chloride to form C-N bond, displacing Cl. In retrosynthesis, we need to break C-N bond and form C-Cl (halide). So we need a template that breaks a secondary amine (C-N) and forms a halide. The functional groups broken: secondary amine? Actually the C-N bond is a secondary amine (if the nitrogen is attached to carbon and maybe other groups). The product has a secondary amine (the given molecule has an aniline? Let's examine SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We have a secondary amide (NC(=O)...). Also there is a side chain: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. That includes a benzylic carbon attached to N4CC(F)C4 (a tertiary amine). The C-N bond of interest likely is the benzylic carbon attached to the nitrogen of the piperazine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a azetidine? Wait N4CC(F)C4 is a four-membered ring with N and F substituent. The CN4... is a secondary amine (benzyl amine). So the C-N bond is a secondary amine (benzyl attached to N of azetidine). The SN2 would be substitution of a halide on that benzylic carbon by the nitrogen nucleophile. So retrosynthesis: replace that C-N bond with C-Cl (or other halide). So we need a template that breaks secondary amine and forms halide.

Search with functional_groups_broken: ["secondary amines"], functional_groups_formed: ["halide"] gave empty. Maybe need to specify "secondary amine" singular? The list includes "secondary amines". Already used. Could also include "alkyl halide" as formed? But halide is generic. Let's try broken: ["secondary amines"], formed: ["alkyl halide"].
